claims.rule: When refactoring Acyclic's Scala 2/3 port, separate compiler tree/symbol/unit extraction and reporter operations from the shared Value/Node graph pipeline; compare the existing file, package, force and skipped cases across both adapters before asserting semantic equivalence.
claims.applicability: Observed review guidance in PR 136 and its implemented revision. The extension to a full parity matrix is an inference. Applies to this compiler plugin's Scala 2/3 architecture, not a requirement to introduce Ox, Cats Effect, ZIO or generic type classes into unrelated Scala applications.
claims.counterexample: Sharing raw compiler symbols or using one phase adapter for both compilers would erase real API and invocation differences. Package-internal cycles permitted by acyclic.pkg are not automatically failures and must not be tightened during a purported behavior-preserving extraction.

claims.rule: For whole-compilation analysis entered through compiler callbacks, test a multi-file cyclic consumer without verbose logging and assert raw diagnostic multiplicity, supplemental dependency locations and line numbering separately from graph membership. Establish the compiler-run lifetime before choosing a guard reset policy.
claims.applicability: The missing messages and duplicate invocation were observed and repaired in PR 136. Reused-instance and raw-event assertions are research inferences prompted by the flag location and set-based test helper, not historical reviewer requirements or proven historical fixes.
claims.counterexample: An idempotence guard is inappropriate for an analysis intentionally performed once per compilation unit. Conversely, a plugin-instance Boolean is not automatically safe for multiple compiler runs, even if the original two-file case produces a single diagnostic.

claims.rule: When reviewing Acyclic diagnostic tests, trace make and the complete subsequent expression: assert a computed exists predicate, preserve the actual diagnostic severity mapping, and distinguish successful compilation from successful warning detection.
claims.applicability: Directly supported by the 2022 warning test and PR 136's 2024 repair. A mutation that removes or changes the expected warning is a proposed validation exercise, not a Scala test executed during this research run.
claims.counterexample: Do not demand a redundant outer Boolean assertion around makeFail: it already intercepts CompilationException and asserts cycle inclusion internally. Its separate weakness is erased multiplicity, not the absence of any assertion.

claims.rule: Inference: preserve the current-unit membership guard when refactoring dependency extraction, and report clean-build coverage separately from incremental runs; a dependency outside the unit map must not become an unchecked map lookup or evidence of whole-project acyclicity.
claims.applicability: Source observation plus an explicit historical documentation limitation. Applies to Acyclic's compilation-run graph. No review was found prescribing this exact membership guard, and no clean or incremental compilation was performed here.
claims.counterexample: An incremental run touching only one side of a source cycle can lack the full graph; accepting that result as a whole-project proof is unsound. A different analyzer with a persistent complete dependency graph need not share this limitation.

claims.rule: In Acyclic revisions that self-apply a released plugin, keep the unreleased-version exclusion minimal and synchronized with release availability, and prevent the published plugin from pre-checking intentionally cyclic test resources before the harness loads the implementation under test.
claims.applicability: The stale exclusion correction is explicit review guidance from PR 123; test isolation is an inference supported by PR 54 and the build/harness sources. This only applies where self-application exists. The examined late-2024 build removed the production bootstrap dependency, so its absence must not be flagged as a stale exclusion defect.
claims.counterexample: Keeping Scala 2.13.13 excluded after its matching plugin release exists weakens self-checking unnecessarily. Conversely, demanding a bootstrap artifact for a not-yet-published compiler target would prevent bootstrapping that release at all.
